You are the Lead Editorial Director for "Rise & Shine (RAS) by KeilHQ" —
"What happened. Why it matters." A high-signal editorial brand for founders,
builders, developers and investors, India-first but globally aware.

Your job: turn a news topic (or pasted news) into a publication-grade RAS
social graphic (single story post OR carousel), then publish it to Instagram
only after the user approves.

## PIPELINE
1. UNDERSTAND & RESEARCH
   - If the user pastes news text, use it directly.
   - If they give a topic, use exaSearch (category "news" for breaking items;
     set startPublishedDate when recency matters) to find sources, then
     exaScrape the best 1-3 URLs for full text. Never invent facts or sources.
   - web_fetch is a cheap fallback for a single known URL.

2. DECIDE THE FORMAT
   - SINGLE story post: when the story is one clear thesis that fits one frame.
   - CAROUSEL (4-5 slides): when there is a genuine multi-point breakdown
     (what changed, why now, the mechanism, second-order effects, the takeaway).
   - If the user explicitly asked for single or carousel, honor that. Otherwise
     pick the one that fits the material and briefly say why.

3. WRITE THE COPY (RAS editorial voice)
   - Headline: a sharp editorial THESIS, not a press-release title.
     GOOD: "Anthropic isn't just building AI. It's building the workforce."
     BAD:  "Anthropic Announces $100M Claude Academy Program"
   - Context deck: exactly 3 short lines. deckLead (line 1) and deckTail
     (line 3) are plain ink; deckHighlight (line 2) is the single emphasized
     phrase shown in the accent color. Keep each line tight (fits one row).
   - Strip any HTML tags or markup from every copy field — plain text only.
   - Pick an accent color by domain:
       #2F7C74 AI & Research · #E2A72E Funding & Deals ·
       #C7E84A Emerging/Future · #F25C3D Urgent/Breaking.
   - Keep ALL on-image text to safe Latin characters. Never use arrows (→),
     triangles, or emoji in on-image fields — the brand fonts can't render them.

4. CHOOSE THE HERO IMAGE (preview, then ask the user)
   - First, gather the candidate hero image(s): any image the user provided
     (path or URL), and/or a relevant one you found on the web via
     exaSearch/exaScrape (get the DIRECT image URL ending in .png/.jpg/.webp).
   - PREVIEW EVERY CANDIDATE INLINE before asking. In a chat message, render
     each candidate as its own Markdown image on its own line so the user can
     SEE it, not just read a URL:
         Candidate A (The Verge): ![candidate A](https://.../image.png)
         Candidate B (OpenAI):    ![candidate B](https://.../image.png)
     Paste the direct image URL verbatim inside the ![...](...) — never show a
     bare URL as the only reference, always embed it as a Markdown image.
   - THEN call ask_user to let the user pick which candidate to use (or provide
     their own). Keep the option labels short (e.g. "Candidate A", "Candidate B",
     "I'll provide my own"); the images are already shown above the question.
   - Use the user's answer as the heroImage. For a carousel, preview and pick
     images for any 'body' slides the same way (reuse the hero or more web images).
   - Only pass a DIRECT image URL (ends in .png/.jpg/.webp) or a local path to
     the render tool.

5. RENDER
   - Single: call render-ras-story with a slug + the structured copy + heroImage.
   - Carousel: call render-ras-carousel with a deckSlug, a cover, and 3-4 slides
     (each 'body' with its own image, or 'text' only). Slide 1 is the cover.
   - Both return assets with view_url/download_url and absolute paths.

6. DELIVER IN CHAT
   - Show every rendered slide inline, in order, by pasting its view_url
     VERBATIM inside a Markdown image: ![alt text](view_url). The view_url the
     render tool returns is already a full absolute URL
     (e.g. http://localhost:4111/ras-assets/<slug>/01.png) — never shorten it,
     strip the scheme, or drop the leading part. One image per line.
   - Then present the Instagram CAPTION and HASHTAGS you wrote (these are
     separate from the on-image text — write a strong caption in RAS voice plus
     5-10 relevant hashtags).

7. PUBLISH (only on explicit approval)
   - NEVER post automatically. Only publish when the user explicitly says to.
   - On the first publish of a session, call checkInstagramConnection first and
     report the account + remaining daily quota (or what config is missing).
   - Then call publish-ras-to-instagram with the ordered view_urls, the

You are the Lead Editorial Director for "Rise & Shine (RAS) by KeilHQ" —
"What happened. Why it matters." A high-signal editorial brand for founders,
builders, developers and investors, India-first but globally aware.

Your job: turn a news topic (or pasted news) into a publication-grade RAS
social graphic (single story post OR carousel), then publish it to Instagram
only after the user approves.

## PIPELINE
1. UNDERSTAND & RESEARCH
   - If the user pastes news text, use it directly.
   - If they give a topic, use exaSearch (category "news" for breaking items;
     set startPublishedDate when recency matters) to find sources, then
     exaScrape the best 1-3 URLs for full text. Never invent facts or sources.
   - web_fetch is a cheap fallback for a single known URL.

2. DECIDE THE FORMAT
   - SINGLE story post: when the story is one clear thesis that fits one frame.
   - CAROUSEL (4-5 slides): when there is a genuine multi-point breakdown
     (what changed, why now, the mechanism, second-order effects, the takeaway).
   - If the user explicitly asked for single or carousel, honor that. Otherwise
     pick the one that fits the material and briefly say why.

3. WRITE THE COPY (RAS editorial voice)
   - Headline: a sharp editorial THESIS, not a press-release title.
     GOOD: "Anthropic isn't just building AI. It's building the workforce."
     BAD:  "Anthropic Announces $100M Claude Academy Program"
   - Context deck: exactly 3 short lines. deckLead (line 1) and deckTail
     (line 3) are plain ink; deckHighlight (line 2) is the single emphasized
     phrase shown in the accent color. Keep each line tight (fits one row).
   - Strip any HTML tags or markup from every copy field — plain text only.
   - Pick an accent color by domain:
       #2F7C74 AI & Research · #E2A72E Funding & Deals ·
       #C7E84A Emerging/Future · #F25C3D Urgent/Breaking.
   - Keep ALL on-image text to safe Latin characters. Never use arrows (→),
     triangles, or emoji in on-image fields — the brand fonts can't render them.

4. CHOOSE THE HERO IMAGE (preview, then ask the user)
   - First, gather the candidate hero image(s): any image the user provided
     (path or URL), and/or a relevant one you found on the web via
     exaSearch/exaScrape (get the DIRECT image URL ending in .png/.jpg/.webp).
   - PREVIEW EVERY CANDIDATE INLINE before asking. In a chat message, render
     each candidate as its own Markdown image on its own line so the user can
     SEE it, not just read a URL:
         Candidate A (The Verge): ![candidate A](https://.../image.png)
         Candidate B (OpenAI):    ![candidate B](https://.../image.png)
     Paste the direct image URL verbatim inside the ![...](...) — never show a
     bare URL as the only reference, always embed it as a Markdown image.
   - THEN call ask_user to let the user pick which candidate to use (or provide
     their own). Keep the option labels short (e.g. "Candidate A", "Candidate B",
     "I'll provide my own"); the images are already shown above the question.
   - Use the user's answer as the heroImage. For a carousel, preview and pick
     images for any 'body' slides the same way (reuse the hero or more web images).
   - Only pass a DIRECT image URL (ends in .png/.jpg/.webp) or a local path to
     the render tool.

5. RENDER
   - Single: call render-ras-story with a slug + the structured copy + heroImage.
   - Carousel: call render-ras-carousel with a deckSlug, a cover, and 3-4 slides
     (each 'body' with its own image, or 'text' only). Slide 1 is the cover.
   - Both return assets with view_url/download_url and absolute paths.

6. DELIVER IN CHAT
   - Show every rendered slide inline, in order, by pasting its view_url
     VERBATIM inside a Markdown image: ![alt text](view_url). The view_url the
     render tool returns is already a full absolute URL
     (e.g. http://localhost:4111/ras-assets/<slug>/01.png) — never shorten it,
     strip the scheme, or drop the leading part. One image per line.
   - Then present the Instagram CAPTION and HASHTAGS you wrote (these are
     separate from the on-image text — write a strong caption in RAS voice plus
     5-10 relevant hashtags).

7. PUBLISH (only on explicit approval)
   - NEVER post automatically. Only publish when the user explicitly says to.
   - On the first publish of a session, call checkInstagramConnection first and
     report the account + remaining daily quota (or what config is missing).
   - Then call publish-ras-to-instagram with the ordered view_urls, the
     caption, and hashtags. This tool pauses for your approval before a real
     post; approve/decline in Studio. In dry-run it reports the payload without
     posting — tell the user it was a dry run and how to go live.
   - Report the returned permalink (or media id) on success.

## TOOLS
- exaSearch / exaScrape: live web research. web_fetch: single-URL fallback.
- ask_user: ask which hero image to use (and any genuine clarification).
- render-ras-story / render-ras-carousel: produce the PNG(s).
- checkInstagramConnection: verify the IG account before publishing.
- publish-ras-to-instagram: approval-gated publish (single or carousel).

Try Claude
  1. Introduction
  2. Performance
  3. Pricing
  4. Safety
  5. Availability
  6. Further updates

October 7, 2026

Claude Haiku 5.5

  1. (1)Performance
  2. (2)Pricing
  3. (3)Safety
  4. (4)Further updates

Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5: the cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model we’ve ever released.

Claude Haiku 5.5 is designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks. It reliably handles quick and repetitive workloads (like summaries, compactions, database queries, and classification requests). It pairs well with Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 as a subagent on coding work. And, since it’s also our fastest model to date, it works especially well for speed-sensitive tasks like live customer support and browser use.¹

Haiku 5.5 is available at a much lower price than Haiku 4.5. On average, it now costs around 75% less to run.²

Along with this launch, we’re making improvements to the value of our model range. We’re halving the price of Claude Sonnet 5.5’s cache reads, which means Sonnet 5.5 now runs around 20% cheaper on most agentic work. And we’re introducing a new monthly API credit for our Claude Max and Team subscribers, designed to support our users in building new agents and applications that run on the Claude Platform.

Performance

Here’s how Claude Haiku 5.5 performs across a range of benchmarks:

Haiku 5.5 is our first Haiku-class model to come with an adjustable effort setting. This means that, as with our other models, users can decide whether to optimize for cost or intelligence. The charts below show how Haiku 5.5 performs on three benchmarks at each effort setting:

Computer use: OSWorldKnowledge work: GDPval-AAMultidisciplinary reasoning: Humanity’s Last Exam

In early testing, our customers reported results consistent with the performance and cost improvements shown above. Here’s what they told us about the new model:

AsanaHubSpotAlphaSenseBoxRogoCognition
Quote

“We’re very impressed with Claude Haiku 5.5, particularly its speed. We ran it through our eval suite for AI Teammates, our AI agent product, covering use cases like triaging bugs, setting up projects, and searching large portfolios to surface high-risk or overdue work. Compared with the model we use today, we saw over a 30% reduction in latency for task completions and up to 2.5x faster inference per agent turn. It’s a noticeably snappier experience.”

CompanyAsana
AuthorAaron Vinh, Staff Software Engineer
Quote

“At HubSpot, we use simulated portals to evaluate new models on CRM tasks like reporting on deals. We mostly test the smaller, more efficient models, and Claude Haiku 5.5 got the best score we’ve seen on this suite yet, at 92.8% averaged over three runs. One CRM audit task asks models to identify stale but ambiguous records. Across all of the models we tested, Haiku 5.5 was fastest to complete the task, and had the highest hit rate and the lowest false positive rate.”

CompanyHubSpot
AuthorZe’ev Klapow, Distinguished Software Engineer
Quote

“Ask in Document is one of our big sources of spend, doing about 8M calls a week in production. It answers very specific questions on top of one or a few documents. We ran 400 queries, and Claude Haiku 5.5 was a statistically significant improvement over Haiku 4.5: 0.84 vs. 0.76.”

CompanyAlphaSense
AuthorDaniel Campos, Distinguished Engineer
Quote

“Our customers use Box AI across large volumes of their enterprise content. With widespread usage comes the need to manage efficiency and cost, and to find the best model to suit the task at hand. In early testing, Claude Haiku 5.5 scored 11 points higher than Haiku 4.5 at about half the latency. We’d put it to use on analytical work that runs at scale, from cost reports to financial summaries and weekly recurring reviews.”

CompanyBox
AuthorYashodha Bhavnani, VP of AI Products
Quote

“The short and high-volume work is where Claude Haiku 5.5 fits for us, like quick lookups, subagents, and summaries. While a bigger model builds the deck, a Haiku 5.5 subagent goes into the 10-K and pulls the segment revenue line the deck needs. It’s accurate enough that we’d trust it there, and fast and cheap enough that we can run it a lot.”

CompanyRogo
AuthorAlex Wang, Applied AI
Quote

“Claude Haiku 5.5 joins the sidekick lineup in Devin Fusion as an excellent option. With Haiku 5.5 as the sidekick, Fusion holds a top-tier FrontierCode score of 66.2 while cutting cost and latency. You can try it today in the Devin CLI with Opus 5.5 as the lead.”

CompanyCognition
AuthorWalden Yan, Co-Founder & CPO

Pricing

The table below shows how Claude Haiku 5.5’s pricing compares to our other models. Haiku 5.5 is especially good value when used for tasks with prompts up to 100,000 tokens, which make up around 90% of requests to our previous Haiku model.

Price per 1 million tokensHaiku 5.5
prompts up to / over 100k		Haiku 4.5Sonnet 5.5
Cache reads$0.01 / $0.05$0.10$0.10
Cache writes$0.125 / $0.625$1.25$2.50
Input tokens$0.10 / $0.50$1.00$2.00
Output tokens$0.50 / $2.50$5.00$10.00

Safety

Alignment. Claude Haiku 5.5 shows major improvements across almost all of our alignment evaluations relative to Haiku 4.5. In particular, we found far fewer instances of misaligned behavior, and a lower willingness to cooperate with misuse. The model’s system card describes our evaluation process and results in more detail.

Safeguards. Consistent with its capabilities, Haiku 5.5’s cybersecurity safeguards are more restrictive than Haiku 4.5’s, but somewhat less restrictive than those we’ve applied to other recent models. In cybersecurity, they permit a wider range of defensive tasks than our safeguards for Sonnet 5.5, but they still block penetration testing and other techniques more likely to be used by attackers.

Haiku 5.5’s biology safeguards are the same as for Sonnet 5, Sonnet 5.5, and Opus 5. They allow research biology questions but restrict access to requests that we judge as likely to cause harm. Organizations working on wider-ranging biology and cyber activities can apply to our Life Sciences Verification Program and Cyber Verification Program.

Availability

Claude Haiku 5.5 is available now on all platforms, including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. On the Claude Platform, developers can get started with claude-haiku-5-5.

See our migration guide for details.

Further updates

Alongside our new pricing for Claude Haiku 5.5, we’re making further improvements to the value of our models and products.

First, starting today, we’re lowering the price of cache reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5. Cache reads now cost 50% less: $0.10 per million tokens rather than $0.20. Because cache reads make up a large share of models’ token consumption, this reduces the cost of Sonnet 5.5 on most agentic tasks by around 20%.

For instance, here’s what the price cut means for Sonnet 5.5’s performance relative to cost on Terminal-Bench 4.0:

Sonnet 5.5 cache reads were cut 50% the same day, and Max/Team plans get monthly API credits.\n\nAnthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 on Oct 7, 2026, completing the Claude 5.5 family after Opus 5.5 (Sep 22) and Sonnet 5.5 (Sep 28). It is aimed at high-volume, cost-sensitive work: summaries, context compaction, database queries, classification, and subagent tasks alongside Opus or Sonnet on coding. Anthropic calls it its fastest model at standard speed, which suits live customer support and browser use.\n\nIt is the first Haiku with adjustable effort (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) and adaptive thinking, and it uses the newer tokenizer shared with Sonnet and Opus 5.5. Claude Code v2.1.293 makes `claude-haiku-5-5` the default Haiku on the Anthropic API with a 1M context window.\n\nOn Anthropic's published table it scores 72.4% on the OSWorld 2.1 offline subset (Haiku 4.5: 15.7%, GPT-6 Luna: 48.9%), 39.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (Haiku 4.5: 0.0%), 46.4% on FrontierCode 1.1 Main, 45.9% / 57.4% on Humanity's Last Exam without / with tools, and 1620 on GDPval-AA v2.1. Anthropic still recommends Sonnet or Opus for complex agentic coding.\n\nPricing for prompts up to 100K tokens is $0.10 input, $0.50 output and $0.01 cache reads per million tokens ($0.50 / $2.50 above 100K), which Anthropic estimates at about 75% cheaper than Haiku 4.5 on average. It is available on the Claude Platform, AWS, Google Cloud and Azure, and on Vercel AI Gateway as `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5`. The same day, Sonnet 5.5 cache reads dropped 50% to $0.10/M, and Max 5x, Max 20x and Team subscribers get $100, $200 and up to $500 in monthly API credits. Per the [official terms](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17154008-monthly-api-credits-for-max-and-team-plans), Team credits are $20/$100 per seat, pooled; they cover the Claude API, Managed Agents, and the Agent SDK, not interactive Claude Code, and do not roll over (claimable after 7 days on the plan).","image":["https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/images/4zrzovbb/website/89e9b0fbfe0181f6ca565d913686ce8e49b5e9c2-1200x630.jpg","https://aicoder.com/favicon.ico"],"inLanguage":"en-US","articleSection":"model","datePublished":"2026-10-07T18:10:20Z","dateModified":"2026-10-07T18:10:20Z","isPartOf":{"@type":"CollectionPage","@id":"https://aicoder.com/news","name":"AI Coding Live News"},"author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Anthropic","url":"https://x.com/AnthropicAI","jobTitle":"AI Researcher / Contributor"},"publisher":{"@type":"Organization","name":"AICoder","url":"https://aicoder.com","logo":{"@type":"ImageObject","url":"https://aicoder.com/favicon.ico","width":64,"height":64}},"keywords":"model-launch, anthropic, claude, haiku, pricing, subagent, computer-use"},{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"BreadcrumbList","itemListElement":[{"@type":"ListItem","position":1,"name":"Home","item":"https://aicoder.com"},{"@type":"ListItem","position":2,"name":"News","item":"https://aicoder.com/news"},{"@type":"ListItem","position":3,"name":"Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5: $0.10/M input, 72.4% on OSWorld 2.1, about 75% cheaper than Haiku 4.5 on average","item":"https://aicoder.com/news/news-20261008-anthropic-claude-haiku-5-5-launch"}]}]</script>

October 7, 2026

Claude Haiku 5.5

  1. (1)Performance
  2. (2)Pricing
  3. (3)Safety
  4. (4)Further updates

Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5: the cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model we’ve ever released.

Claude Haiku 5.5 is designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks. It reliably handles quick and repetitive workloads (like summaries, compactions, database queries, and classification requests). It pairs well with Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 as a subagent on coding work. And, since it’s also our fastest model to date, it works especially well for speed-sensitive tasks like live customer support and browser use.¹

Haiku 5.5 is available at a much lower price than Haiku 4.5. On average, it now costs around 75% less to run.²

Along with this launch, we’re making improvements to the value of our model range. We’re halving the price of Claude Sonnet 5.5’s cache reads, which means Sonnet 5.5 now runs around 20% cheaper on most agentic work. And we’re introducing a new monthly API credit for our Claude Max and Team subscribers, designed to support our users in building new agents and applications that run on the Claude Platform.

Performance

Here’s how Claude Haiku 5.5 performs across a range of benchmarks:

Haiku 5.5 is our first Haiku-class model to come with an adjustable effort setting. This means that, as with our other models, users can decide whether to optimize for cost or intelligence. The charts below show how Haiku 5.5 performs on three benchmarks at each effort setting:

Computer use: OSWorldKnowledge work: GDPval-AAMultidisciplinary reasoning: Humanity’s Last Exam

In early testing, our customers reported results consistent with the performance and cost improvements shown above. Here’s what they told us about the new model:

AsanaHubSpotAlphaSenseBoxRogoCognition
Quote

“We’re very impressed with Claude Haiku 5.5, particularly its speed. We ran it through our eval suite for AI Teammates, our AI agent product, covering use cases like triaging bugs, setting up projects, and searching large portfolios to surface high-risk or overdue work. Compared with the model we use today, we saw over a 30% reduction in latency for task completions and up to 2.5x faster inference per agent turn. It’s a noticeably snappier experience.”

CompanyAsana
AuthorAaron Vinh, Staff Software Engineer
Quote

“At HubSpot, we use simulated portals to evaluate new models on CRM tasks like reporting on deals. We mostly test the smaller, more efficient models, and Claude Haiku 5.5 got the best score we’ve seen on this suite yet, at 92.8% averaged over three runs. One CRM audit task asks models to identify stale but ambiguous records. Across all of the models we tested, Haiku 5.5 was fastest to complete the task, and had the highest hit rate and the lowest false positive rate.”

CompanyHubSpot
AuthorZe’ev Klapow, Distinguished Software Engineer
Quote

“Ask in Document is one of our big sources of spend, doing about 8M calls a week in production. It answers very specific questions on top of one or a few documents. We ran 400 queries, and Claude Haiku 5.5 was a statistically significant improvement over Haiku 4.5: 0.84 vs. 0.76.”

CompanyAlphaSense
AuthorDaniel Campos, Distinguished Engineer
Quote

“Our customers use Box AI across large volumes of their enterprise content. With widespread usage comes the need to manage efficiency and cost, and to find the best model to suit the task at hand. In early testing, Claude Haiku 5.5 scored 11 points higher than Haiku 4.5 at about half the latency. We’d put it to use on analytical work that runs at scale, from cost reports to financial summaries and weekly recurring reviews.”

CompanyBox
AuthorYashodha Bhavnani, VP of AI Products
Quote

“The short and high-volume work is where Claude Haiku 5.5 fits for us, like quick lookups, subagents, and summaries. While a bigger model builds the deck, a Haiku 5.5 subagent goes into the 10-K and pulls the segment revenue line the deck needs. It’s accurate enough that we’d trust it there, and fast and cheap enough that we can run it a lot.”

CompanyRogo
AuthorAlex Wang, Applied AI
Quote

“Claude Haiku 5.5 joins the sidekick lineup in Devin Fusion as an excellent option. With Haiku 5.5 as the sidekick, Fusion holds a top-tier FrontierCode score of 66.2 while cutting cost and latency. You can try it today in the Devin CLI with Opus 5.5 as the lead.”

CompanyCognition
AuthorWalden Yan, Co-Founder & CPO

Pricing

The table below shows how Claude Haiku 5.5’s pricing compares to our other models. Haiku 5.5 is especially good value when used for tasks with prompts up to 100,000 tokens, which make up around 90% of requests to our previous Haiku model.

Price per 1 million tokensHaiku 5.5
prompts up to / over 100k		Haiku 4.5Sonnet 5.5
Cache reads$0.01 / $0.05$0.10$0.10
Cache writes$0.125 / $0.625$1.25$2.50
Input tokens$0.10 / $0.50$1.00$2.00
Output tokens$0.50 / $2.50$5.00$10.00

Safety

Alignment. Claude Haiku 5.5 shows major improvements across almost all of our alignment evaluations relative to Haiku 4.5. In particular, we found far fewer instances of misaligned behavior, and a lower willingness to cooperate with misuse. The model’s system card describes our evaluation process and results in more detail.

Safeguards. Consistent with its capabilities, Haiku 5.5’s cybersecurity safeguards are more restrictive than Haiku 4.5’s, but somewhat less restrictive than those we’ve applied to other recent models. In cybersecurity, they permit a wider range of defensive tasks than our safeguards for Sonnet 5.5, but they still block penetration testing and other techniques more likely to be used by attackers.

Haiku 5.5’s biology safeguards are the same as for Sonnet 5, Sonnet 5.5, and Opus 5. They allow research biology questions but restrict access to requests that we judge as likely to cause harm. Organizations working on wider-ranging biology and cyber activities can apply to our Life Sciences Verification Program and Cyber Verification Program.

Availability

Claude Haiku 5.5 is available now on all platforms, including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. On the Claude Platform, developers can get started with claude-haiku-5-5.

See our migration guide for details.

Further updates

Alongside our new pricing for Claude Haiku 5.5, we’re making further improvements to the value of our models and products.

First, starting today, we’re lowering the price of cache reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5. Cache reads now cost 50% less: $0.10 per million tokens rather than $0.20. Because cache reads make up a large share of models’ token consumption, this reduces the cost of Sonnet 5.5 on most agentic tasks by around 20%.

Sonnet 5.5 cache reads were cut 50% the same day, and Max/Team plans get monthly API credits.\n\nAnthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 on Oct 7, 2026, completing the Claude 5.5 family after Opus 5.5 (Sep 22) and Sonnet 5.5 (Sep 28). It is aimed at high-volume, cost-sensitive work: summaries, context compaction, database queries, classification, and subagent tasks alongside Opus or Sonnet on coding. Anthropic calls it its fastest model at standard speed, which suits live customer support and browser use.\n\nIt is the first Haiku with adjustable effort (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) and adaptive thinking, and it uses the newer tokenizer shared with Sonnet and Opus 5.5. Claude Code v2.1.293 makes `claude-haiku-5-5` the default Haiku on the Anthropic API with a 1M context window.\n\nOn Anthropic's published table it scores 72.4% on the OSWorld 2.1 offline subset (Haiku 4.5: 15.7%, GPT-6 Luna: 48.9%), 39.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (Haiku 4.5: 0.0%), 46.4% on FrontierCode 1.1 Main, 45.9% / 57.4% on Humanity's Last Exam without / with tools, and 1620 on GDPval-AA v2.1. Anthropic still recommends Sonnet or Opus for complex agentic coding.\n\nPricing for prompts up to 100K tokens is $0.10 input, $0.50 output and $0.01 cache reads per million tokens ($0.50 / $2.50 above 100K), which Anthropic estimates at about 75% cheaper than Haiku 4.5 on average. It is available on the Claude Platform, AWS, Google Cloud and Azure, and on Vercel AI Gateway as `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5`. The same day, Sonnet 5.5 cache reads dropped 50% to $0.10/M, and Max 5x, Max 20x and Team subscribers get $100, $200 and up to $500 in monthly API credits. Per the [official terms](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17154008-monthly-api-credits-for-max-and-team-plans), Team credits are $20/$100 per seat, pooled; they cover the Claude API, Managed Agents, and the Agent SDK, not interactive Claude Code, and do not roll over (claimable after 7 days on the plan).","image":["https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/images/4zrzovbb/website/89e9b0fbfe0181f6ca565d913686ce8e49b5e9c2-1200x630.jpg","https://aicoder.com/favicon.ico"],"inLanguage":"en-US","articleSection":"model","datePublished":"2026-10-07T18:10:20Z","dateModified":"2026-10-07T18:10:20Z","isPartOf":{"@type":"CollectionPage","@id":"https://aicoder.com/news","name":"AI Coding Live News"},"author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Anthropic","url":"https://x.com/AnthropicAI","jobTitle":"AI Researcher / Contributor"},"publisher":{"@type":"Organization","name":"AICoder","url":"https://aicoder.com","logo":{"@type":"ImageObject","url":"https://aicoder.com/favicon.ico","width":64,"height":64}},"keywords":"model-launch, anthropic, claude, haiku, pricing, subagent, computer-use"},{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"BreadcrumbList","itemListElement":[{"@type":"ListItem","position":1,"name":"Home","item":"https://aicoder.com"},{"@type":"ListItem","position":2,"name":"News","item":"https://aicoder.com/news"},{"@type":"ListItem","position":3,"name":"Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5: $0.10/M input, 72.4% on OSWorld 2.1, about 75% cheaper than Haiku 4.5 on average","item":"https://aicoder.com/news/news-20261008-anthropic-claude-haiku-5-5-launch"}]}]</script>

You are the Lead Editorial Director for "Rise & Shine (RAS) by KeilHQ" —
"What happened. Why it matters." A high-signal editorial brand for founders,
builders, developers and investors, India-first but globally aware.

Your job: turn a news topic (or pasted news) into a publication-grade RAS
social graphic (single story post OR carousel), then publish it to Instagram
only after the user approves.

## PIPELINE
1. UNDERSTAND & RESEARCH
   - If the user pastes news text, use it directly.
   - If they give a topic, use exaSearch (category "news" for breaking items;
     set startPublishedDate when recency matters) to find sources, then
     exaScrape the best 1-3 URLs for full text. Never invent facts or sources.
   - web_fetch is a cheap fallback for a single known URL.

2. DECIDE THE FORMAT
   - SINGLE story post: when the story is one clear thesis that fits one frame.
   - CAROUSEL (4-5 slides): when there is a genuine multi-point breakdown
     (what changed, why now, the mechanism, second-order effects, the takeaway).
   - If the user explicitly asked for single or carousel, honor that. Otherwise
     pick the one that fits the material and briefly say why.

3. WRITE THE COPY (RAS editorial voice)
   - Headline: a sharp editorial THESIS, not a press-release title.
     GOOD: "Anthropic isn't just building AI. It's building the workforce."
     BAD:  "Anthropic Announces $100M Claude Academy Program"
   - Context deck: exactly 3 short lines. deckLead (line 1) and deckTail
     (line 3) are plain ink; deckHighlight (line 2) is the single emphasized
     phrase shown in the accent color. Keep each line tight (fits one row).
   - Strip any HTML tags or markup from every copy field — plain text only.
   - Pick an accent color by domain:
       #2F7C74 AI & Research · #E2A72E Funding & Deals ·
       #C7E84A Emerging/Future · #F25C3D Urgent/Breaking.
   - Keep ALL on-image text to safe Latin characters. Never use arrows (→),
     triangles, or emoji in on-image fields — the brand fonts can't render them.

4. CHOOSE THE HERO IMAGE (preview, then ask the user)
   - First, gather the candidate hero image(s): any image the user provided
     (path or URL), and/or a relevant one you found on the web via
     exaSearch/exaScrape (get the DIRECT image URL ending in .png/.jpg/.webp).
   - PREVIEW EVERY CANDIDATE INLINE before asking. In a chat message, render
     each candidate as its own Markdown image on its own line so the user can
     SEE it, not just read a URL:
         Candidate A (The Verge): ![candidate A](https://.../image.png)
         Candidate B (OpenAI):    ![candidate B](https://.../image.png)
     Paste the direct image URL verbatim inside the ![...](...) — never show a
     bare URL as the only reference, always embed it as a Markdown image.
   - THEN call ask_user to let the user pick which candidate to use (or provide
     their own). Keep the option labels short (e.g. "Candidate A", "Candidate B",
     "I'll provide my own"); the images are already shown above the question.
   - Use the user's answer as the heroImage. For a carousel, preview and pick
     images for any 'body' slides the same way (reuse the hero or more web images).
   - Only pass a DIRECT image URL (ends in .png/.jpg/.webp) or a local path to
     the render tool.

5. RENDER
   - Single: call render-ras-story with a slug + the structured copy + heroImage.
   - Carousel: call render-ras-carousel with a deckSlug, a cover, and 3-4 slides
     (each 'body' with its own image, or 'text' only). Slide 1 is the cover.
   - Both return assets with view_url/download_url and absolute paths.

6. DELIVER IN CHAT
   - Show every rendered slide inline, in order, by pasting its view_url
     VERBATIM inside a Markdown image: ![alt text](view_url). The view_url the
     render tool returns is already a full absolute URL
     (e.g. http://localhost:4111/ras-assets/<slug>/01.png) — never shorten it,
     strip the scheme, or drop the leading part. One image per line.
   - Then present the Instagram CAPTION and HASHTAGS you wrote (these are
     separate from the on-image text — write a strong caption in RAS voice plus
     5-10 relevant hashtags).

7. PUBLISH (only on explicit approval)
   - NEVER post automatically. Only publish when the user explicitly says to.
   - On the first publish of a session, call checkInstagramConnection first and
     report the account + remaining daily quota (or what config is missing).
   - Then call publish-ras-to-instagram with the ordered view_urls, the
     caption, and hashtags. This tool pauses for your approval before a real
     post; approve/decline in Studio. In dry-run it reports the payload without
     posting — tell the user it was a dry run and how to go live.
   - Report the returned permalink (or media id) on success.

## TOOLS
- exaSearch / exaScrape: live web research. web_fetch: single-URL fallback.
- ask_user: ask which hero image to use (and any genuine clarification).
- render-ras-story / render-ras-carousel: produce the PNG(s).
- checkInstagramConnection: verify the IG account before publishing.
- publish-ras-to-instagram: approval-gated publish (single or carousel).

Be concise and editorial. Research first, never fabricate, and always get image
choice + publish approval from the user.

Try Claude
  1. Introduction
  2. Performance
  3. Pricing
  4. Safety
  5. Availability
  6. Further updates

October 7, 2026

Claude Haiku 5.5

  1. (1)Performance
  2. (2)Pricing
  3. (3)Safety
  4. (4)Further updates

Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5: the cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model we’ve ever released.

Claude Haiku 5.5 is designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks. It reliably handles quick and repetitive workloads (like summaries, compactions, database queries, and classification requests). It pairs well with Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 as a subagent on coding work. And, since it’s also our fastest model to date, it works especially well for speed-sensitive tasks like live customer support and browser use.¹

Haiku 5.5 is available at a much lower price than Haiku 4.5. On average, it now costs around 75% less to run.²

Along with this launch, we’re making improvements to the value of our model range. We’re halving the price of Claude Sonnet 5.5’s cache reads, which means Sonnet 5.5 now runs around 20% cheaper on most agentic work. And we’re introducing a new monthly API credit for our Claude Max and Team subscribers, designed to support our users in building new agents and applications that run on the Claude Platform.

Performance

Here’s how Claude Haiku 5.5 performs across a range of benchmarks:

Haiku 5.5 is our first Haiku-class model to come with an adjustable effort setting. This means that, as with our other models, users can decide whether to optimize for cost or intelligence. The charts below show how Haiku 5.5 performs on three benchmarks at each effort setting:

Computer use: OSWorldKnowledge work: GDPval-AAMultidisciplinary reasoning: Humanity’s Last Exam

In early testing, our customers reported results consistent with the performance and cost improvements shown above. Here’s what they told us about the new model:

AsanaHubSpotAlphaSenseBoxRogoCognition
Quote

“We’re very impressed with Claude Haiku 5.5, particularly its speed. We ran it through our eval suite for AI Teammates, our AI agent product, covering use cases like triaging bugs, setting up projects, and searching large portfolios to surface high-risk or overdue work. Compared with the model we use today, we saw over a 30% reduction in latency for task completions and up to 2.5x faster inference per agent turn. It’s a noticeably snappier experience.”

CompanyAsana
AuthorAaron Vinh, Staff Software Engineer
Quote

“At HubSpot, we use simulated portals to evaluate new models on CRM tasks like reporting on deals. We mostly test the smaller, more efficient models, and Claude Haiku 5.5 got the best score we’ve seen on this suite yet, at 92.8% averaged over three runs. One CRM audit task asks models to identify stale but ambiguous records. Across all of the models we tested, Haiku 5.5 was fastest to complete the task, and had the highest hit rate and the lowest false positive rate.”

CompanyHubSpot
AuthorZe’ev Klapow, Distinguished Software Engineer
Quote

“Ask in Document is one of our big sources of spend, doing about 8M calls a week in production. It answers very specific questions on top of one or a few documents. We ran 400 queries, and Claude Haiku 5.5 was a statistically significant improvement over Haiku 4.5: 0.84 vs. 0.76.”

CompanyAlphaSense
AuthorDaniel Campos, Distinguished Engineer
Quote

“Our customers use Box AI across large volumes of their enterprise content. With widespread usage comes the need to manage efficiency and cost, and to find the best model to suit the task at hand. In early testing, Claude Haiku 5.5 scored 11 points higher than Haiku 4.5 at about half the latency. We’d put it to use on analytical work that runs at scale, from cost reports to financial summaries and weekly recurring reviews.”

CompanyBox
AuthorYashodha Bhavnani, VP of AI Products
Quote

“The short and high-volume work is where Claude Haiku 5.5 fits for us, like quick lookups, subagents, and summaries. While a bigger model builds the deck, a Haiku 5.5 subagent goes into the 10-K and pulls the segment revenue line the deck needs. It’s accurate enough that we’d trust it there, and fast and cheap enough that we can run it a lot.”

CompanyRogo
AuthorAlex Wang, Applied AI
Quote

“Claude Haiku 5.5 joins the sidekick lineup in Devin Fusion as an excellent option. With Haiku 5.5 as the sidekick, Fusion holds a top-tier FrontierCode score of 66.2 while cutting cost and latency. You can try it today in the Devin CLI with Opus 5.5 as the lead.”

CompanyCognition
AuthorWalden Yan, Co-Founder & CPO

Pricing

The table below shows how Claude Haiku 5.5’s pricing compares to our other models. Haiku 5.5 is especially good value when used for tasks with prompts up to 100,000 tokens, which make up around 90% of requests to our previous Haiku model.

Price per 1 million tokensHaiku 5.5
prompts up to / over 100k		Haiku 4.5Sonnet 5.5
Cache reads$0.01 / $0.05$0.10$0.10
Cache writes$0.125 / $0.625$1.25$2.50
Input tokens$0.10 / $0.50$1.00$2.00
Output tokens$0.50 / $2.50$5.00$10.00

Safety

Alignment. Claude Haiku 5.5 shows major improvements across almost all of our alignment evaluations relative to Haiku 4.5. In particular, we found far fewer instances of misaligned behavior, and a lower willingness to cooperate with misuse. The model’s system card describes our evaluation process and results in more detail.

Safeguards. Consistent with its capabilities, Haiku 5.5’s cybersecurity safeguards are more restrictive than Haiku 4.5’s, but somewhat less restrictive than those we’ve applied to other recent models. In cybersecurity, they permit a wider range of defensive tasks than our safeguards for Sonnet 5.5, but they still block penetration testing and other techniques more likely to be used by attackers.

Haiku 5.5’s biology safeguards are the same as for Sonnet 5, Sonnet 5.5, and Opus 5. They allow research biology questions but restrict access to requests that we judge as likely to cause harm. Organizations working on wider-ranging biology and cyber activities can apply to our Life Sciences Verification Program and Cyber Verification Program.

Availability

Claude Haiku 5.5 is available now on all platforms, including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. On the Claude Platform, developers can get started with claude-haiku-5-5.

See our migration guide for details.

Further updates

Alongside our new pricing for Claude Haiku 5.5, we’re making further improvements to the value of our models and products.

First, starting today, we’re lowering the price of cache reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5. Cache reads now cost 50% less: $0.10 per million tokens rather than $0.20. Because cache reads make up a large share of models’ token consumption, this reduces the cost of Sonnet 5.5 on most agentic tasks by around 20%.

It targets high-volume, cost-sensitive work such as summaries, compaction, classification and coding subagents, and Anthropic calls it its fastest model at standard speed. Prompts up to 100K cost $0.10 input / $0.50 output per million tokens, and it is the first Haiku with effort levels. It scores 72.4% on the OSWorld 2.1 offline subset (Haiku 4.5: 15.7%) and 39.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0. Sonnet 5.5 cache reads were cut 50% the same day, and Max/Team plans get monthly API credits.\n\nAnthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 on Oct 7, 2026, completing the Claude 5.5 family after Opus 5.5 (Sep 22) and Sonnet 5.5 (Sep 28). It is aimed at high-volume, cost-sensitive work: summaries, context compaction, database queries, classification, and subagent tasks alongside Opus or Sonnet on coding. Anthropic calls it its fastest model at standard speed, which suits live customer support and browser use.\n\nIt is the first Haiku with adjustable effort (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) and adaptive thinking, and it uses the newer tokenizer shared with Sonnet and Opus 5.5. Claude Code v2.1.293 makes `claude-haiku-5-5` the default Haiku on the Anthropic API with a 1M context window.\n\nOn Anthropic's published table it scores 72.4% on the OSWorld 2.1 offline subset (Haiku 4.5: 15.7%, GPT-6 Luna: 48.9%), 39.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (Haiku 4.5: 0.0%), 46.4% on FrontierCode 1.1 Main, 45.9% / 57.4% on Humanity's Last Exam without / with tools, and 1620 on GDPval-AA v2.1. Anthropic still recommends Sonnet or Opus for complex agentic coding.\n\nPricing for prompts up to 100K tokens is $0.10 input, $0.50 output and $0.01 cache reads per million tokens ($0.50 / $2.50 above 100K), which Anthropic estimates at about 75% cheaper than Haiku 4.5 on average. It is available on the Claude Platform, AWS, Google Cloud and Azure, and on Vercel AI Gateway as `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5`. The same day, Sonnet 5.5 cache reads dropped 50% to $0.10/M, and Max 5x, Max 20x and Team subscribers get $100, $200 and up to $500 in monthly API credits. Per the [official terms](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17154008-monthly-api-credits-for-max-and-team-plans), Team credits are $20/$100 per seat, pooled; they cover the Claude API, Managed Agents, and the Agent SDK, not interactive Claude Code, and do not roll over (claimable after 7 days on the plan).","image":["https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/images/4zrzovbb/website/89e9b0fbfe0181f6ca565d913686ce8e49b5e9c2-1200x630.jpg","https://aicoder.com/favicon.ico"],"inLanguage":"en-US","articleSection":"model","datePublished":"2026-10-07T18:10:20Z","dateModified":"2026-10-07T18:10:20Z","isPartOf":{"@type":"CollectionPage","@id":"https://aicoder.com/news","name":"AI Coding Live News"},"author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Anthropic","url":"https://x.com/AnthropicAI","jobTitle":"AI Researcher / Contributor"},"publisher":{"@type":"Organization","name":"AICoder","url":"https://aicoder.com","logo":{"@type":"ImageObject","url":"https://aicoder.com/favicon.ico","width":64,"height":64}},"keywords":"model-launch, anthropic, claude, haiku, pricing, subagent, computer-use"},{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"BreadcrumbList","itemListElement":[{"@type":"ListItem","position":1,"name":"Home","item":"https://aicoder.com"},{"@type":"ListItem","position":2,"name":"News","item":"https://aicoder.com/news"},{"@type":"ListItem","position":3,"name":"Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5: $0.10/M input, 72.4% on OSWorld 2.1, about 75% cheaper than Haiku 4.5 on average","item":"https://aicoder.com/news/news-20261008-anthropic-claude-haiku-5-5-launch"}]}]</script>

contents.title: Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5 \ Anthropic
contents.text:
Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5 \ Anthropic

October 7, 2026

# Claude Haiku 5.5

Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5: the cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model we’ve ever released.

Claude Haiku 5.5 is designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks. It reliably handles quick and repetitive workloads (like summaries, compactions, database queries, and classification requests). It pairs well with Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 as a subagent on coding work. And, since it’s also our fastest model to date, it works especially well for speed-sensitive tasks like live customer support and browser use.¹

Haiku 5.5 is available at a much lower price than Haiku 4.5. On average, it now costs around 75% less to run.²

Along with this launch, we’re making improvements to the value of our model range. We’re halving the price of Claude Sonnet 5.5’s cache reads, which means Sonnet 5.5 now runs around 20% cheaper on most agentic work. And we’re introducing a new monthly API credit for our Claude Max and Team subscribers, designed to support our users in building new agents and applications that run on the Claude Platform.

## Performance

Here’s how Claude Haiku 5.5 performs across a range of benchmarks:

| Knowledge work GDPval-AA v2.1 | | | | |

| Knowledge work AA-Briefcase v1.1 | | | | |
| Knowledge work AA-Briefcase v1.1 | 1578 | 614 | 1336 | 1824 |
| Computer use OSWorld 2.1 | | | | |
| Computer use OSWorld 2.1 | 72.4% Offline subset | 15.7% Offline subset | 48.9% Offline subset | 83.9% Offline subset |
| Multidisciplinary reasoning Humanity’s Last Exam | | | | |
| Multidisciplinary reasoning Humanity’s Last Exam | 45.9% no tools | 10.2% no tools | — | 56.9% no tools |
| | 57.4% with tools | 18.7% with tools | — | 64.5% with tools |
| Agentic coding Terminal-Bench 4.0 | | | | |
| Agentic coding Terminal-Bench 4.0 | 39.2% | 0.0% | 16.4% | 70.6% |
| Agentic coding FrontierCode 1.1 (Main) | | | | |
| Agentic coding FrontierCode 1.1 (Main) | 46.4% | — | 42.4% | 52.1% Xhigh |
| Visual reasoning Chartography | | | | |
| Visual reasoning Chartography | 46.4% no tools | 6.4% no tools | 29.1% no tools | 61.6% no tools |

For details on how we run our evaluations, see the Haiku 5.5 System Card.

Haiku 5.5 is our first Haiku-class model to come with an adjustable effort setting. This means that, as with our other models, users can decide whether to optimize for cost or intelligence. The charts below show how Haiku 5.5 performs on three benchmarks at each effort setting:

Computer use: OSWorld Knowledge work: GDPval-AA Multidisciplinary reasoning: Humanity’s Last Exam

OSWorld 2.1 (offline subset) Accuracy vs. cost

- Haiku 5.5
- Haiku 4.5
- Sonnet 5.5
- GPT-6 Luna

OSWorld 2.1 measures how well agents can operate a real computer to finish long, multi-step tasks.

GDPval-AA v2.1 Accuracy vs. cost

- Haiku 5.5
- Haiku 4.5
- Sonnet 5.5
- GPT-6 Luna

Artificial Analysis’s GDPval-AA v2.1 evaluates agents on real-world professional work across 44 occupations.

Humanity’s Last Exam (no tools) Accuracy vs. cost

- Haiku 5.5
- Haiku 4.5
- Sonnet 5.5

Humanity’s Last Exam (HLE) is a test of expert-level academic knowledge and reasoning.

In early testing, our customers reported results consistent with the performance and cost improvements shown above. Here’s what they told us about the new model:

> “We’re very impressed with Claude Haiku 5.5, particularly its speed. We ran it through our eval suite for AI Teammates, our AI agent product, covering use cases like triaging bugs, setting up projects, and searching large portfolios to surface high-risk or overdue work. Compared with the model we use today, we saw over a 30% reduction in latency for task completions and up to 2.5x faster inference per agent turn. It’s a noticeably snappier experience.”

Company Asana Author Aaron Vinh, Staff Software Engineer

> “At HubSpot, we use simulated portals to evaluate new models on CRM tasks like reporting on deals. We mostly test the smaller, more efficient models, and Claude Haiku 5.5 got the best score we’ve seen on this suite yet, at 92.8% averaged over three runs. One CRM audit task asks models to identify stale but ambiguous records. Across all of the models we tested, Haiku 5.5 was fastest to complete the task, and had the highest hit rate and the lowest false positive rate.”

Company HubSpot Author Ze’ev Klapow, Distinguished Software Engineer

> “Ask in Document is one of our big sources of spend, doing about 8M calls a week in production. It answers very specific questions on top of one or a few documents. We ran 400 queries, and Claude Haiku 5.5 was a statistically significant improvement over Haiku 4.5: 0.84 vs. 0.76.”

Company AlphaSense Author Daniel Campos, Distinguished Engineer

> “Our customers use Box AI across large volumes of their enterprise content. With widespread usage comes the need to manage efficiency and cost, and to find the best model to suit the task at hand. In early testing, Claude Haiku 5.5 scored 11 points higher than Haiku 4.5 at about half the latency. We’d put it to use on analytical work that runs at scale, from cost reports to financial summaries and weekly recurring reviews.”

Company Box Author Yashodha Bhavnani, VP of AI Products

> “The short and high-volume work is where Claude Haiku 5.5 fits for us, like quick lookups, subagents, and summaries. While a bigger model builds the deck, a Haiku 5.5 subagent goes into the 10-K and pulls the segment revenue line the deck needs. It’s accurate enough that we’d trust it there, and fast and cheap enough that we can run it a lot.”

> “Claude Haiku 5.5 joins the sidekick lineup in Devin Fusion as an excellent option. With Haiku 5.5 as the sidekick, Fusion holds a top-tier FrontierCode score of 66.2 while cutting cost and latency. You can try it today in the Devin CLI with Opus 5.5 as the lead.”

## Pricing

The table below shows how Claude Haiku 5.5’s pricing compares to our other models. Haiku 5.5 is especially good value when used for tasks with prompts up to 100,000 tokens, which make up around 90% of requests to our previous Haiku model.

| Price per 1 million tokens | Haiku 5.5 prompts up to / over 100k | Haiku 4.5 | Sonnet 5.5 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cache reads | $0.01 / $0.05 | $0.10 | $0.10 |
| Cache writes | $0.125 / $0.625 | $1.25 | $2.50 |
| Input tokens | $0.10 / $0.50 | $1.00 | $2.00 |
| Output tokens | $0.50 / $2.50 | $5.00 | $10.00 |

## Safety

Alignment. Claude Haiku 5.5 shows major improvements across almost all of our alignment evaluations relative to Haiku 4.5. In particular, we found far fewer instances of misaligned behavior, and a lower willingness to cooperate with misuse. The model’s system card describes our evaluation process and results in more detail.

Safeguards. Consistent with its capabilities, Haiku 5.5’s cybersecurity safeguards are more restrictive than Haiku 4.5’s, but somewhat less restrictive than those we’ve applied to other recent models. In cybersecurity, they permit a wider range of defensive tasks than our safeguards for Sonnet 5.5, but they still block penetration testing and other techniques more likely to be used by attackers.

Haiku 5.5’s biology safeguards are the same as for Sonnet 5, Sonnet 5.5, and Opus 5. They allow research biology questions but restrict access to requests that we judge as likely to cause harm. Organizations working on wider-ranging biology and cyber activities can apply to our Life Sciences Verification Program and Cyber Verification Program.

## Availability

Claude Haiku 5.5 is available now on all platforms, including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. On the Claude Platform, developers can get started with `claude-haiku-5-5`. 

See our migration guide for details.

You are the Lead Editorial Director for "Rise & Shine (RAS) by KeilHQ" —
"What happened. Why it matters." A high-signal editorial brand for founders,
builders, developers and investors, India-first but globally aware.

Your job: turn a news topic (or pasted news) into a publication-grade RAS
social graphic (single story post OR carousel), then publish it to Instagram
only after the user approves.

## PIPELINE
1. UNDERSTAND & RESEARCH
   - If the user pastes news text, use it directly.
   - If they give a topic, use exaSearch (category "news" for breaking items;
     set startPublishedDate when recency matters) to find sources, then
     exaScrape the best 1-3 URLs for full text. Never invent facts or sources.
   - web_fetch is a cheap fallback for a single known URL.

2. DECIDE THE FORMAT
   - SINGLE story post: when the story is one clear thesis that fits one frame.
   - CAROUSEL (4-5 slides): when there is a genuine multi-point breakdown
     (what changed, why now, the mechanism, second-order effects, the takeaway).
   - If the user explicitly asked for single or carousel, honor that. Otherwise
     pick the one that fits the material and briefly say why.

3. WRITE THE COPY (RAS editorial voice)
   - Headline: a sharp editorial THESIS, not a press-release title.
     GOOD: "Anthropic isn't just building AI. It's building the workforce."
     BAD:  "Anthropic Announces $100M Claude Academy Program"
   - Context deck: exactly 3 short lines. deckLead (line 1) and deckTail
     (line 3) are plain ink; deckHighlight (line 2) is the single emphasized
     phrase shown in the accent color. Keep each line tight (fits one row).
   - Strip any HTML tags or markup from every copy field — plain text only.
   - Pick an accent color by domain:
       #2F7C74 AI & Research · #E2A72E Funding & Deals ·
       #C7E84A Emerging/Future · #F25C3D Urgent/Breaking.
   - Keep ALL on-image text to safe Latin characters. Never use arrows (→),
     triangles, or emoji in on-image fields — the brand fonts can't render them.

4. CHOOSE THE HERO IMAGE (preview, then ask the user)
   - First, gather the candidate hero image(s): any image the user provided
     (path or URL), and/or a relevant one you found on the web via
     exaSearch/exaScrape (get the DIRECT image URL ending in .png/.jpg/.webp).
   - PREVIEW EVERY CANDIDATE INLINE before asking. In a chat message, render
     each candidate as its own Markdown image on its own line so the user can
     SEE it, not just read a URL:
         Candidate A (The Verge): ![candidate A](https://.../image.png)
         Candidate B (OpenAI):    ![candidate B](https://.../image.png)
     Paste the direct image URL verbatim inside the ![...](...) — never show a
     bare URL as the only reference, always embed it as a Markdown image.
   - THEN call ask_user to let the user pick which candidate to use (or provide
     their own). Keep the option labels short (e.g. "Candidate A", "Candidate B",
     "I'll provide my own"); the images are already shown above the question.
   - Use the user's answer as the heroImage. For a carousel, preview and pick
     images for any 'body' slides the same way (reuse the hero or more web images).
   - Only pass a DIRECT image URL (ends in .png/.jpg/.webp) or a local path to
     the render tool.

5. RENDER
   - Single: call render-ras-story with a slug + the structured copy + heroImage.
   - Carousel: call render-ras-carousel with a deckSlug, a cover, and 3-4 slides
     (each 'body' with its own image, or 'text' only). Slide 1 is the cover.
   - Both return assets with view_url/download_url and absolute paths.

6. DELIVER IN CHAT
   - Show every rendered slide inline, in order, by pasting its view_url
     VERBATIM inside a Markdown image: ![alt text](view_url). The view_url the
     render tool returns is already a full absolute URL
     (e.g. http://localhost:4111/ras-assets/<slug>/01.png) — never shorten it,
     strip the scheme, or drop the leading part. One image per line.
   - Then present the Instagram CAPTION and HASHTAGS you wrote (these are
     separate from the on-image text — write a strong caption in RAS voice plus
     5-10 relevant hashtags).

7. PUBLISH (only on explicit approval)
   - NEVER post automatically. Only publish when the user explicitly says to.
   - On the first publish of a session, call checkInstagramConnection first and
     report the account + remaining daily quota (or what config is missing).
   - Then call publish-ras-to-instagram with the ordered view_urls, the
     caption, and hashtags. This tool pauses for your approval before a real
     post; approve/decline in Studio. In dry-run it reports the payload without
     posting — tell the user it was a dry run and how to go live.
   - Report the returned permalink (or media id) on success.

## TOOLS
- exaSearch / exaScrape: live web research. web_fetch: single-URL fallback.
- ask_user: ask which hero image to use (and any genuine clarification).
- render-ras-story / render-ras-carousel: produce the PNG(s).
- checkInstagramConnection: verify the IG account before publishing.
- publish-ras-to-instagram: approval-gated publish (single or carousel).

Be concise and editorial. Research first, never fabricate, and always get image
choice + publish approval from the user.
